filterCurves.description: Configuration recipes for FLEX's Master Filter (Bottom Left) to create mixing tools and special effects.

filter_types_explained.Low Pass: Removes high frequencies - makes sound darker/warmer
filter_types_explained.High Pass: Removes low frequencies - makes sound thinner/cleaner
filter_types_explained.Band Pass: Only allows middle frequencies - telephone/radio effect
filter_types_explained.Notch: Removes a specific frequency band - surgical cut
filter_types_explained.Peak: Boosts a specific frequency band - emphasis
filter_types_explained.Phaser: Creates sweeping phase cancellation - psychedelic effect
filter_types_explained.All Pass: Changes phase without affecting frequency - subtle structural changes

curves.name: The Clean-Up (High Pass)
curves.description: Removes unnecessary low frequencies from non-bass instruments.
curves.sonic_character: Cleaner, tighter, removes mud and rumble
when_to_use: Pads to make room for bass
Removing rumble from any non-bass sound
automation_ideas: Start at 80Hz, sweep to 200Hz during build-ups
tips: Sweep up until sound gets thin, then back off slightly
Be careful with pianos - don't cut too much
Use 6dB slope for gentle cut, 24dB for aggressive
curves.before_after: Before: Muddy, competing with bass. After: Clean, clear, focused

curves.name: Telephone / Radio
curves.description: Isolates the midrange for a lo-fi communication device sound.
curves.sonic_character: Thin, nasal, lo-fi, vintage communication device
when_to_use: Intro effects before full sound drops
automation_ideas: Automate from Band Pass to Off (bypass) for dramatic reveal
Sweep cutoff 800Hz to 3kHz for scanning radio effect
tips: Combine with bit crusher or distortion for more degradation
Works great on vocals and keys
Lower cutoff (800Hz) = older phone, higher (2kHz) = modern
curves.before_after: Before: Full range. After: Tinny, narrow, vintage

curves.name: Acid Squelch
automation_ideas: CRITICAL: Automate cutoff constantly - static acid is boring
Fast cutoff sweeps (16th notes) for classic acid
Slow sweeps for building tension
tips: High resonance (70-90%) is essential
24dB slope is critical for authentic sound
Combine with Limiter 'Distortion' for more grit
curves.before_after: Before: Static bass. After: Squelchy, animated, aggressive
curves.warning: High resonance can cause piercing frequencies - watch levels

curves.name: Talkbox Vowel
curves.description: Imparts a vocal quality to the sound through formant filtering.
automation_ideas: Automate cutoff 0-100% = cycles through vowel sounds (A-E-I-O-U)
Step automation for rhythmic talking effect
Slow sweep for evolving vocal character
tips: Move cutoff slowly to hear different vowels
Works best on harmonically rich sounds
Combine with slight distortion for more character
curves.before_after: Before: Normal synth. After: Sounds like it's singing/talking

curves.name: Phaser Wash
curves.description: Adds swirling phase cancellation movement to static sounds.
automation_ideas: Sine wave automation on cutoff for classic phaser sweep
Increase resonance during builds for more intensity
Random LFO for unpredictable movement
tips: Phaser 1 = subtle, Phaser 2 = medium, Phaser 3 = intense
Higher resonance = more pronounced effect
Use slow automation (4-8 bars) for best results
curves.before_after: Before: Static. After: Swirling, moving, spacey

curves.name: Anti-Fizz (Low Pass)
curves.description: Tames harsh digital high frequencies without muffling the sound.
curves.sonic_character: Smoother highs, less digital harshness, more analog feel
when_to_use: Bright sawtooth synths that are too harsh
Presets with too much high-end sizzle
automation_ideas: Open up to 12kHz during chorus/drop for more energy
Close down to 6kHz for verses/quieter sections
tips: 6dB slope is key - gentle and natural
Don't go below 7kHz or sound gets muffled
Use instead of EQ for more natural sound
curves.before_after: Before: Harsh, digital, fatiguing. After: Smooth, warm, pleasant

curves.name: Sub Bass Isolator
curves.description: Removes everything except sub frequencies for powerful low end.
curves.sonic_character: Pure sub bass, no harmonics, floor-shaking
automation_ideas: Automate cutoff from 80Hz to 200Hz for bass that growls up
tips: Keep this layer MONO - critical for club systems
Layer with mid bass (200Hz+) for complete bass sound
Use 24dB slope for clean cutoff
curves.before_after: Before: Full bass. After: Pure sub frequencies only

curves.name: Air Filter (High Shelf)
curves.description: Simulates high shelf EQ for adding air and presence.
automation_ideas: Increase resonance to 50% during chorus for lift
tips: Don't overdo it - can get harsh quickly
Works best on already-bright sounds
Combine with Limiter 'Warming' to control harshness
curves.before_after: Before: Dull. After: Bright, airy, sparkly

curves.name: Notch Sweep
curves.description: Sweeping notch creates dramatic movement and tension.
automation_ideas: Sweep from low to high over 8 bars for build-up
Fast sweeps (1 bar) for dramatic effect
Step automation for glitchy sounds
tips: High resonance makes the sweep more obvious
Works great on white noise and full mixes
Combine with reverb automation for bigger effect
curves.before_after: Before: Static. After: Sweeping, moving, dramatic

curves.name: Comb Metallic
curves.description: Creates metallic, robotic, or alien-like sounds through comb filtering.
curves.frequency_target: Creates series of notches for metallic quality
automation_ideas: Automate cutoff for tuned metallic notes
Subtle movement adds character
tips: Comb+ and Comb- sound different - try both
Works best on harmonically rich sounds
Small cutoff movements create big changes
curves.before_after: Before: Normal synth. After: Metallic, robotic, unusual

curves.name: Lo-Fi Muffler
curves.description: Aggressive low pass for heavy lo-fi character.
automation_ideas: Automate from 1kHz to 8kHz for dramatic open-up
Keep low during verses, open for chorus
tips: Combine with Limiter 'Warming' for vintage sound
Lower cutoff (1-2kHz) for extreme lo-fi
Add noise/crackle macros if available
curves.before_after: Before: Modern, bright. After: Vintage, muffled, nostalgic

workflow_tips: Start with Master Filter OFF - only add if needed
Static filters are for mixing, animated filters are for effects
High Pass everything except bass and kick
Low Pass to remove digital harshness
automation_workflow: 1. Right-click Cutoff knob → Create automation clip
2. Draw your automation curve (sweeps, steps, etc.)
3. Adjust Resonance for more dramatic sweeps
4. A/B test to ensure it's not too extreme
common_mistakes: Too much high pass - sound gets thin
Too much low pass - sound gets muffled
Forgetting to automate - filter just sits there
Too much resonance - causes painful peaks
Using steep slopes when gentle would work better

genre_quick_reference.Drops: Low Pass @ 8kHz, open to full during drop
